today.title: Today
today.note: Your consistency, this week's call and today's list arrive in M4.

train.title: Train
train.note: Sessions and sets arrive in M4.

progress.title: Progress
progress.note: Photos, strength and projection arrive in M6.

data_insufficient.title: Not yet. More weigh-ins first.
data_insufficient.body: One morning is mostly water. A few regular mornings show the trend, and the trend is what the call is made on.

window_not_full.title: Not yet. Your plan needs its full window.
window_not_full.body: Keep going as planned. Judging it early would read water and daily swings as progress or as a stall.

wait_one_more_week.title: Hold steady one more week.
wait_one_more_week.body: Your weight has only just paused. One flat week is usually water, and the change tends to show up all at once. Nothing changes yet.

check_in_needed_training.title: How is training going?
check_in_needed_training.body: Before any change to food, the coach needs to know whether your lifts are holding up. Log this week's sessions or answer the training question, and the call follows.

check_in_needed_recovery.title: How are you recovering?
check_in_needed_recovery.body: Your weight is moving the right way and training is holding. One question about sleep and energy decides whether anything should change.

check_in_needed_adherence.title: How much of the plan happened?
check_in_needed_adherence.body: Your weight isn't moving yet. Whether that calls for a new plan depends on how much of this one happened. Log the week and the call follows.

calorie_change_too_soon.title: Give the new target time to work.
calorie_change_too_soon.body: Your calories changed recently. A new target needs a couple of weeks before the scale can say anything about it.

observing.title: First, finding your real maintenance.
observing.body: Your starting calories are an estimate, and estimates miss by a few hundred either way. For the first weeks the plan stays put while your weigh-ins show what your body actually needs.

loss_rate_cap.title: You're losing faster than your body can keep up with.
loss_rate_cap.body: Past this pace you start losing muscle, and the extra on the scale is mostly water. Calories go up a step this week so what you lose stays fat.

rapid_loss.title: You've lost a lot in a short time. Time to ease off.
rapid_loss.body: The scale has been dropping faster than a steady pace for a while now. Calories go up a step so your body keeps up and what you lose stays fat.

low_energy_availability.title: Your plan leaves too little fuel for your training.
low_energy_availability.body: After what your workouts burn, what's left is less than your body needs to run well. Calories go up so training, sleep and recovery have enough to work with.

bmr_floor.title: Food stays where it is. Movement goes up.
bmr_floor.body: Another calorie cut would take you under what your body needs at rest. More daily steps get the same result without eating less.

carb_squeeze.title: Food stays where it is. Movement goes up.
carb_squeeze.body: A lower target would leave too little room for protein and the carbs your training runs on. More daily steps get the same result without eating less.

menstrual_loss_reported.title: Your plan pauses here.
menstrual_loss_reported.body: A change in your cycle is a sign your body needs more fuel. No more eating under your needs: calories stay at least at maintenance, and it's worth talking to your doctor about it.

bulk_ceiling.title: Time to switch to a cut.
bulk_ceiling.body: Past this point, more food mostly adds fat rather than muscle. A cut now makes the next bulk count.

fat_first.title: Lose fat first.
fat_first.body: Muscle you build now would stay hidden. Most people start here, and a cut first makes every later gain visible.

surplus_zone.title: Time to switch to a bulk.
surplus_zone.body: You're lean enough that cutting further costs more than it gives. Building from here is the next step.

plateau.title: Keep the same weight this week.
plateau.body: The lifts that stalled keep the same weight for a week before anything else changes.

load_held_still_stalled.title: A lighter week.
load_held_still_stalled.body: Holding the weight didn't move things, so this week has fewer sets. A lighter week often gives your body room to recover.

long_stagnation.title: A lighter week.
long_stagnation.body: Months at the same weights often mean tiredness has built up. This week has fewer sets; after it, build back up gradually.

plan_missed.title: Take this week off from the gym.
plan_missed.body: For a while now the plan hasn't gone the way it was written. A lighter week rarely fixes that; a full week away does. Come back gradually after it.

loads_regressed.title: Look at food and sleep first.
loads_regressed.body: This week you couldn't lift what you lifted last week. Going backwards is rarely about the training itself: check how you ate and slept, one thing at a time.

recovery_poor.title: Your training is fine. Your recovery isn't.
recovery_poor.body: The work is getting done but you're not bouncing back. Protein and sleep come first this week; food amounts stay the same.

toward_goal.title: Keep going exactly as you are.
toward_goal.body: Your weight is moving the right way and nothing says it needs help. Changing a plan that works only adds noise.

energy_floor.title: Calories stay where they are.
energy_floor.body: Going lower would leave too little fuel after your training. Progress may be slower from here, and that's the safe side to be on.

adherence_low.title: The plan comes first, not a new plan.
adherence_low.body: Less than half of the plan happened over the last few weeks. Changing calories now would change a plan that hasn't been tried. Pick the one habit that slipped most and start there.

adherence_partial.title: Close, but not enough to judge the plan yet.
adherence_partial.body: A good part of the plan happened, not quite enough to tell whether it works. Calories stay where they are while the plan gets a fair try.

performance_red_flag.title: Your lifts come first. No calorie cut this week.
performance_red_flag.body: Your training is slipping while your weight isn't moving toward your goal. Cutting more now would cost muscle. Calories stay, and the focus is getting your sessions back on track.

training_first.title: Training first, food decisions later.
training_first.body: Your training is going backwards. Before anything about food changes, look at how you train: rest between sessions, sleep, and not doing too much.

not_toward_goal.title: Time for a new calorie target.
not_toward_goal.body: You followed the plan and your weight hasn't moved the way it should over the last few weeks. One clear step now, then a few weeks to see it work.

genetic_limit.title: Ease the pace a little.
genetic_limit.body: Your weight is moving, training and recovery are fine, but the mirror isn't keeping up. That's the pace your body can use right now, so calories move one step back toward maintenance.

appetite_gone.title: A short cut to bring your appetite back.
appetite_gone.body: After a long bulk, forcing food down means the bulk has stopped paying off. A few weeks of eating a bit under your needs resets your appetite and clears the fat the bulk added; then the bulk picks up again.
